subject: C
topic: Rapid mixed revision & weak-area drill — GK J&K

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which Mughal Emperor is credited with laying out the famous Shalimar Bagh garden in Srinagar?
questions.explanation: 'Jahangir' is correct — Shalimar Bagh on the banks of Dal Lake was laid out by Emperor Jahangir in 1619 for his wife Nur Jahan. 'Shah Jahan' is wrong — while he later extended some gardens in Kashmir, Shalimar Bagh was originally built by Jahangir. 'Akbar' is wrong — Akbar conquered Kashmir in 1586 but did not build Shalimar Bagh. 'Aurangzeb' is wrong — he reigned after Jahangir and Shah Jahan and was not the garden's creator.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Chenab River in J&K:

(i) It is formed by the confluence of Chandra and Bhaga rivers at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh.
(ii) The Baglihar Dam and Salal Dam are built on the Chenab.
(iii) It flows through the Doda and Kishtwar districts of J&K.
(iv) It is the longest river flowing entirely within J&K.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Chenab is formed by the merger of Chandra and Bhaga rivers at Tandi in Lahaul, Himachal Pradesh. (ii) is correct — both Baglihar (450 MW, Ramban) and Salal (690 MW, Reasi) are on the Chenab. (iii) is correct — the Chenab flows through the mountainous Doda and Kishtwar districts. (iv) is wrong — the Chenab originates in Himachal Pradesh, so it does not flow 'entirely within J&K'; also the Jhelum has a longer course within J&K.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Pir Panjal range separates the Jammu region from the Kashmir Valley.
Reason (R): The Banihal Pass and the Jawahar Tunnel on NH-44 cross the Pir Panjal range to connect Jammu to Srinagar.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Pir Panjal range acts as a physical barrier between the Jammu plains and the Kashmir Valley. (R) is correct — the Banihal Pass and Jawahar Tunnel on NH-44 cross this range. (R) explains (A) because the need for a tunnel/pass to cross this range demonstrates that it separates the two regions. Option 2 is wrong because R directly supports A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following festivals of J&K with the communities that celebrate them:

Column I:
(a) Navroz
(b) Lohri
(c) Eid-ul-Fitr
(d) Baisakhi

Column II:
(i) Sikhs
(ii) Muslims
(iii) Kashmiri Pandits / Shia Muslims
(iv) Dogras / Punjabis

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(iii) is correct — Navroz (Persian New Year) is celebrated by Kashmiri Pandits (as Navreh) and Shia Muslims in J&K. (b)-(iv) is correct — Lohri is celebrated by Dogras and Punjabis in the Jammu region. (c)-(ii) is correct — Eid-ul-Fitr is the Muslim festival marking the end of Ramadan. (d)-(i) is correct — Baisakhi is primarily a Sikh harvest festival. The other options incorrectly match festivals with communities.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The first railway line in J&K (Jammu-Udhampur section) was inaugurated in which year?
questions.explanation: '2005' is correct — the Jammu–Udhampur rail link (55 km) was inaugurated on 13 April 2005. '2000' is wrong — construction was ongoing but the line was not completed until 2005. '2010' is wrong — by this time the Udhampur–Katra extension was under construction. '2014' is wrong — the Udhampur–Katra section was opened in 2014, not the first Jammu–Udhampur line.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following power projects in J&K have a capacity exceeding 400 MW?

(i) Salal HEP (690 MW)
(ii) Uri-I HEP (480 MW)
(iii) Baglihar HEP Stage I (450 MW)
(iv) Lower Jhelum HEP (105 MW)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Salal HEP has a capacity of 690 MW (on Chenab). (ii) is correct — Uri-I HEP has a capacity of 480 MW (on Jhelum). (iii) is correct — Baglihar Stage I has a capacity of 450 MW (on Chenab). (iv) is wrong — Lower Jhelum HEP has only 105 MW capacity, well below 400 MW.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Mughal Road in J&K connects which two districts?
questions.explanation: 'Poonch and Shopian' is correct — the historic Mughal Road (84 km) connects Bufliaz in Poonch district to Shopian in South Kashmir. 'Rajouri and Anantnag' is wrong — while Rajouri is nearby, the road's endpoints are Poonch and Shopian. 'Poonch and Baramulla' is wrong — Baramulla is in North Kashmir, not on this route. 'Rajouri and Budgam' is wrong — Budgam is in central Kashmir and not connected by the Mughal Road.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Dal Lake:

(i) It covers an area of approximately 18 sq km.
(ii) It is divided into parts: Gagribal, Lokut Dal, Bod Dal, and Nagin.
(iii) Houseboats on Dal Lake are a major tourist attraction.
(iv) It is located in Anantnag district.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Dal Lake covers approximately 18 sq km (though it has shrunk over time). (ii) is correct — the lake is divided into these basins/parts. (iii) is correct — the decorated houseboats (shikaras) are iconic tourist attractions. (iv) is wrong — Dal Lake is in Srinagar district, not Anantnag.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The ancient name of Kashmir, 'Kashyapamar', is believed to be derived from the sage __________.
questions.explanation: 'Kashyapa' is correct — according to legend, the Kashmir Valley was once a lake called Satisar, which Sage Kashyapa drained; 'Kashmir' derives from 'Kashyapamar' (the land of Kashyapa). 'Vishwamitra' is wrong — he is associated with the creation of Gayatri Mantra, not Kashmir's naming. 'Vashishtha' is wrong — while an important sage, he is not linked to Kashmir's etymology. 'Agastya' is wrong — he is associated with South India and the Vindhyas, not Kashmir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Karewa deposits in the Kashmir Valley are of great economic importance.
Reason (R): Karewas are lacustrine deposits (ancient lake sediments) that are fertile and suitable for saffron and almond cultivation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Karewa deposits are economically important for horticulture in Kashmir. (R) is correct — Karewas are ancient lake bed deposits rich in fine silt and clay, ideal for growing saffron (in Pampore) and almonds. (R) explains (A) because the fertility of these lacustrine deposits is the direct reason for their economic value. Option 2 is wrong because R causally explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is geologically and agriculturally correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which of the following national highways passes through the Jawahar Tunnel?
questions.explanation: 'NH-44' is correct — the Jawahar Tunnel (Banihal Tunnel) on the Jammu–Srinagar highway is part of NH-44 (renumbered from the old NH-1A). 'NH-1' is wrong — the new NH numbering system designates the Jammu-Srinagar route as NH-44. 'NH-2' is wrong — NH-2 was the old Delhi-Kolkata highway (now part of other NHs). 'NH-144A' is wrong — this is a different route in J&K connecting Batote to Kishtwar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following districts of J&K with their main crops/products:

Column I:
(a) Pulwama
(b) Baramulla
(c) Kathua
(d) Doda

Column II:
(i) Rice and wheat
(ii) Saffron
(iii) Apples
(iv) Maize and rajma (kidney beans)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(ii) is correct — Pulwama (particularly Pampore) is famous for saffron cultivation. (b)-(iii) is correct — Baramulla (Sopore area) is a major apple-producing district. (c)-(i) is correct — Kathua in the plains is known for rice and wheat cultivation. (d)-(iv) is correct — Doda in the hilly region grows maize and rajma (kidney beans) as key crops. The other options incorrectly pair districts with products.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Raghunath Temple in Jammu was built during the reign of which Dogra ruler?
questions.explanation: 'Maharaja Gulab Singh' is correct — construction of Raghunath Temple began under Maharaja Gulab Singh around 1835 and was completed by his son Maharaja Ranbir Singh. 'Maharaja Ranbir Singh' is wrong — while he completed and expanded it, the construction was initiated by Gulab Singh. 'Maharaja Hari Singh' is wrong — he was the last ruler (1925–1952), long after the temple was built. 'Maharaja Pratap Singh' is wrong — he ruled from 1885 to 1925, after the temple's completion.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the RTI Act in the context of J&K:

(i) The RTI Act, 2005 became applicable to J&K after the reorganization in 2019.
(ii) Before 2019, J&K had its own J&K Right to Information Act, 2009.
(iii) Under the RTI Act, information must be provided within 30 days of the request.
(iv) The Central Information Commission has no jurisdiction over J&K matters.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Central RTI Act, 2005 became applicable to J&K after the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into effect on 31 October 2019. (ii) is correct — J&K earlier had its own RTI Act (2009) under its special status. (iii) is correct — under the RTI Act, 2005, information must ordinarily be provided within 30 days. (iv) is wrong — after reorganization, the Central Information Commission has full jurisdiction over J&K UT.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Tawi River flows through which major city of J&K?
questions.explanation: 'Jammu' is correct — the Tawi River flows through the heart of Jammu city, which is sometimes called 'the city on the banks of Tawi'. 'Srinagar' is wrong — Srinagar is on the banks of the Jhelum River. 'Udhampur' is wrong — Udhampur is situated on the Devika rivulet, not the Tawi. 'Anantnag' is wrong — Anantnag is on the banks of the Jhelum in South Kashmir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Srinagar is known as the 'Venice of the East'.
Reason (R): Srinagar has an extensive network of lakes, waterways, and canals, including Dal Lake and Jhelum River, which are used for transport and livelihood.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Srinagar is popularly called 'Venice of the East' due to its waterways. (R) is correct — the city's lakes (Dal, Nagin), the Jhelum River, and connecting waterways/canals enable water transport. (R) explains (A) because the resemblance to Venice (a city built on waterways) is precisely due to Srinagar's extensive water network. Option 2 is wrong because R gives the direct reason for the name. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are UNESCO-recognized or nominated sites from J&K?

(i) Mughal Gardens (Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh)
(ii) Dachigam National Park
(iii) Shankaracharya Temple
(iv) Martand Sun Temple ruins

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Mughal Gardens of Kashmir have been on India's UNESCO World Heritage tentative list. (iv) is correct — the Martand Sun Temple ruins in Anantnag have been nominated for UNESCO consideration. (ii) is wrong — Dachigam is a national park but is not on the UNESCO heritage list. (iii) is wrong — while historically significant, Shankaracharya Temple is not a UNESCO-recognized site.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Instrument of Accession of J&K to India was signed by Maharaja Hari Singh on which date?
questions.explanation: '26 October 1947' is correct — Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947, following the tribal invasion. '15 August 1947' is wrong — this is India's Independence Day; J&K had not yet acceded. '26 January 1950' is wrong — this is when India became a Republic; accession happened much earlier. '14 November 1947' is wrong — by this date, accession had already taken place.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The famous Hemis Monastery, known for its annual masked dance festival, is located in __________ district.
questions.explanation: 'Leh' is correct — Hemis Monastery is located about 45 km from Leh in the UT of Ladakh (previously part of J&K). 'Srinagar' is wrong — Hemis is far from Srinagar, across the Zoji La in Ladakh. 'Kargil' is wrong — while in the same UT of Ladakh, Hemis is in Leh district, not Kargil. 'Anantnag' is wrong — Anantnag is in the Kashmir Valley, not in Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Kishtwar National Park is primarily known for which animal?
questions.explanation: 'Himalayan Brown Bear' is correct — Kishtwar National Park in Kishtwar district is one of the few habitats of the Himalayan Brown Bear in J&K. 'Hangul' is wrong — the Hangul is primarily found in Dachigam National Park. 'Snow Leopard' is wrong — snow leopards are mainly associated with Hemis National Park in Ladakh. 'Musk Deer' is wrong — while present in the area, the park is primarily known for the endangered brown bear.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tourist destinations in J&K with their main attractions:

Column I:
(a) Gulmarg
(b) Pahalgam
(c) Vaishno Devi
(d) Patnitop

Column II:
(i) Hill station and skiing
(ii) Religious pilgrimage
(iii) Lidder Valley and Betaab Valley
(iv) Plateau hill resort in Jammu region

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(i) is correct — Gulmarg is a hill station famous for Asia's highest gondola and skiing. (b)-(iii) is correct — Pahalgam is known for the Lidder Valley, Betaab Valley, and Aru Valley. (c)-(ii) is correct — Vaishno Devi is one of India's most visited religious pilgrimage sites. (d)-(iv) is correct — Patnitop is a plateau hill resort in Udhampur district, Jammu region. The other options misassign attractions.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the geography of J&K:

(i) The Kashmir Valley lies between the Great Himalayan Range and the Pir Panjal Range.
(ii) The Shivalik Hills form the southernmost mountain range in J&K.
(iii) The highest peak in J&K (including former territory) is K2 (Mount Godwin-Austen).
(iv) The total area of J&K UT is approximately 42,241 sq km.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Kashmir Valley is a tectonic valley lying between the Great Himalayas to the north/east and the Pir Panjal range to the south. (ii) is correct — the Shivalik Hills (also called outer Himalayas) form the southernmost range in J&K near the plains. (iv) is correct — J&K UT has an area of approximately 42,241 sq km (excluding Ladakh UT). (iii) is wrong — K2 is in the Pakistan-administered portion (Gilgit-Baltistan); the highest peak in Indian-administered J&K is not K2.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Shankaracharya Temple in Srinagar is situated on which hill?
questions.explanation: 'Takht-e-Sulaiman (Gopadri Hill)' is correct — the ancient Shankaracharya Temple is perched at 1,000 feet on the Takht-e-Sulaiman hill overlooking Dal Lake. 'Hari Parbat' is wrong — it has its own fort (Hari Parbat Fort) but not the Shankaracharya Temple. 'Zabarwan Hill' is wrong — the Zabarwan range is nearby but the temple is specifically on Takht-e-Sulaiman. 'Mahadev Peak' is wrong — this is in Pahalgam, not Srinagar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The economy of J&K is primarily dependent on horticulture and tourism.
Reason (R): The mountainous terrain limits large-scale industrial development, while the climate and geography favour fruit cultivation and scenic beauty.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — horticulture (apples, saffron, walnuts) and tourism are the twin pillars of J&K's economy. (R) is correct — the mountainous terrain constrains heavy industry, while the temperate climate suits fruit cultivation and the natural beauty attracts tourists. (R) explains (A) because geographic factors both limit industrialization and enable horticulture/tourism. Option 2 is wrong because R gives the causal geographic reasons. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Pangong Lake, which gained fame from the movie '3 Idiots', lies in which region?
questions.explanation: 'Ladakh' is correct — Pangong Tso (Lake) at an altitude of 4,350 m extends from Ladakh (India) into Tibet (China). 'Kashmir Valley' is wrong — Pangong is far from the Valley, across multiple mountain ranges. 'Jammu' is wrong — Jammu division is in the south, far from Ladakh. 'Doda' is wrong — Doda district is in the Chenab Valley, not near Pangong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows tourist arrivals (in lakhs) in J&K over four years:

2019 → 21.1
2020 → 3.2
2021 → 10.8
2022 → 18.9

What is the approximate percentage recovery in tourist numbers from 2020 to 2022?
questions.explanation: Percentage increase from 2020 to 2022 = [(18.9–3.2)/3.2] × 100 = (15.7/3.2) × 100 = 490.6% ≈ 490%. '350%' is wrong — this would require 2022 arrivals of about 14.4 lakhs. '550%' is wrong — this would require 2022 arrivals of about 20.8 lakhs. '280%' is wrong — this would require 2022 arrivals of about 12.2 lakhs.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of Dogra rulers of J&K?

(i) Maharaja Gulab Singh
(ii) Maharaja Ranbir Singh
(iii) Maharaja Pratap Singh
(iv) Maharaja Hari Singh
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order is: Gulab Singh (1846–1857), Ranbir Singh (1857–1885), Pratap Singh (1885–1925), Hari Singh (1925–1952). Option 2 is wrong — Ranbir Singh came before Pratap Singh. Option 3 is wrong — Gulab Singh was the first. Option 4 is wrong — Pratap Singh preceded Hari Singh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements about the climate of J&K are correct?

(i) Srinagar experiences a temperate climate with cold winters and mild summers.
(ii) Jammu has a sub-tropical climate with hot summers.
(iii) Snowfall occurs throughout J&K during winter uniformly.
(iv) The Kashmir Valley receives both winter (western disturbance) and summer (monsoon) rainfall.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Srinagar at ~1,600m has a temperate climate with cold snowy winters and mild summers. (ii) is correct — Jammu in the plains has a sub-tropical climate with hot humid summers. (iv) is correct — Kashmir gets winter precipitation from western disturbances and some monsoon rainfall in summer. (iii) is wrong — snowfall is not uniform; it occurs in higher elevations (Kashmir, mountains) but not in the Jammu plains.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Chashme Shahi garden in Srinagar was built by which Mughal ruler?
questions.explanation: 'Shah Jahan' is correct — Chashme Shahi ('Royal Spring') was built around 1632 by Shah Jahan (or on his orders by Ali Mardan Khan). 'Jahangir' is wrong — he built Shalimar Bagh, not Chashme Shahi. 'Akbar' is wrong — he conquered Kashmir but did not build this garden. 'Humayun' is wrong — he ruled before Kashmir was under Mughal control.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers of J&K with the cities they flow through:

Column I:
(a) Jhelum
(b) Tawi
(c) Lidder
(d) Chenab

Column II:
(i) Pahalgam
(ii) Jammu
(iii) Kishtwar
(iv) Srinagar

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(iv) is correct — the Jhelum flows through Srinagar city. (b)-(ii) is correct — the Tawi flows through Jammu city. (c)-(i) is correct — the Lidder river flows through Pahalgam. (d)-(iii) is correct — the Chenab flows through Kishtwar district. The other options incorrectly pair rivers with cities.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which handicraft of J&K involves intricate hand-embroidery on shawls and is known worldwide?
questions.explanation: 'Sozni (Needlework)' is correct — Sozni embroidery involves fine needle-based hand embroidery on Pashmina and other shawls, making each piece unique and highly valued. 'Papier-mâché' is wrong — it involves making decorative items from paper pulp, not embroidery on shawls. 'Woodcarving' is wrong — walnut wood carving creates furniture and boxes, not shawl embroidery. 'Copper work' is wrong — it involves engraving on copper vessels and utensils.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indus Water Treaty in relation to J&K:

(i) Under the treaty, India can use the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) for limited non-consumptive purposes.
(ii) The treaty allows India to construct run-of-the-river hydroelectric projects on western rivers.
(iii) The Baglihar Dam on Chenab was a subject of dispute under this treaty.
(iv) The treaty gives India unrestricted use of all rivers flowing through J&K.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — India can use western rivers for limited non-consumptive uses (navigation, power generation with restrictions). (ii) is correct — India is permitted to build run-of-the-river (not storage) projects on western rivers. (iii) is correct — Pakistan raised objections about the Baglihar Dam under the treaty's dispute resolution mechanism, resolved by a Neutral Expert in 2007. (iv) is wrong — India does NOT have unrestricted use; the western rivers are allocated primarily to Pakistan with only limited use rights for India.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Amar Mahal Palace in Jammu was built in which architectural style?
questions.explanation: 'French' is correct — the Amar Mahal (now a museum) was built in the 19th century in French architectural style, resembling a French château. 'Mughal' is wrong — Mughal architecture features domes, arches, and gardens, not the château style of Amar Mahal. 'British Colonial' is wrong — while built during the colonial era, its architecture is distinctly French, not British. 'Rajasthani' is wrong — Rajasthani architecture features jharokhas and sandstone, not the Amar Mahal's style.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The data below shows apple production (in lakh metric tonnes) in J&K over three years:

2020–21 → 18.4
2021–22 → 21.7
2022–23 → 23.1

What is the approximate total increase in production from 2020–21 to 2022–23?
questions.explanation: Total increase = 23.1 – 18.4 = 4.7 lakh metric tonnes. '3.3 lakh MT' is wrong — this is the increase from 2020–21 to 2021–22 only. '5.8 lakh MT' is wrong — this overstates the increase. '2.1 lakh MT' is wrong — this would be the increase if production went from only 21.0 to 23.1.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which lake in J&K is known as the 'Supreme Gem of Kashmir Lakes' and is famous for its lotus blooms?
questions.explanation: 'Manasbal Lake' is correct — it is called the 'Supreme Gem of Kashmir Lakes' and is famous for its abundant lotus flowers covering much of its surface. 'Dal Lake' is wrong — while beautiful, it is known as the 'Jewel of Srinagar', not the 'Supreme Gem'. 'Wular Lake' is wrong — it is the largest freshwater lake but not known for lotus blooms. 'Nagin Lake' is wrong — it is adjacent to Dal Lake and known for clear water, not specifically lotus.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sopore in Baramulla district is called 'Apple Town of Kashmir'.
Reason (R): Sopore is one of the largest fruit mandis (markets) in Asia and is the hub of apple trade in J&K.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Sopore is indeed known as the 'Apple Town' of Kashmir. (R) is correct — Sopore houses one of Asia's largest fruit markets and is the major trading hub for Kashmir's apple industry. (R) explains (A) because the massive apple trade and market presence is exactly why Sopore earned this title. Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act was passed by the Indian Parliament in which year?
questions.explanation: '2019' is correct — the J&K Reorganisation Act was passed on 5 August 2019 and came into effect on 31 October 2019, bifurcating J&K into two UTs. '2020' is wrong — the Act was already in effect by 2020. '2018' is wrong — the Act was not conceived until 2019. '2017' is wrong — J&K was still a state under President's Rule in 2017.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following industries are significant in the economy of J&K?

(i) Handicrafts (Pashmina, Papier-mâché, Carpet weaving)
(ii) Horticulture (Apple, Walnut, Saffron)
(iii) Automobile manufacturing
(iv) Sericulture (Silk production)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — handicrafts (Pashmina shawls, papier-mâché, carpet weaving, woodwork) are a significant industry employing lakhs of artisans. (ii) is correct — horticulture (apples, walnuts, saffron, cherries) is a major economic pillar. (iv) is correct — sericulture (silk worm rearing and silk production) has been traditionally practiced in Kashmir. (iii) is wrong — J&K does not have a significant automobile manufacturing industry due to its mountainous terrain and limited industrial infrastructure.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Nishat Bagh garden in Srinagar was built by:
questions.explanation: 'Asaf Khan' is correct — Nishat Bagh ('Garden of Bliss') was built in 1633 by Asaf Khan, the elder brother of Empress Nur Jahan and father of Mumtaz Mahal. 'Emperor Jahangir' is wrong — he built Shalimar Bagh, not Nishat Bagh. 'Emperor Shah Jahan' is wrong — he built Chashme Shahi, not Nishat Bagh. 'Zain-ul-Abidin' is wrong — he was a medieval Kashmir sultan (1420–1470), centuries before the Mughal gardens were built.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Bahu Fort in Jammu is situated on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation: 'Tawi' is correct — Bahu Fort, one of the oldest structures in Jammu city, is perched on a rocky cliff on the left bank of the Tawi River. 'Chenab' is wrong — the Chenab flows through Akhnoor and Kishtwar, not through Jammu city where Bahu Fort stands. 'Ravi' is wrong — the Ravi flows along the southern border of J&K, not through Jammu city. 'Jhelum' is wrong — the Jhelum flows through the Kashmir Valley, far from Jammu.
